About our guardians, about how we each had our own collection chests under our beds, the football, the rounders, the little path that took you all round the outside of the main house, round all its nooks and crannies, the duck pond, the food, the view from the Art Room over the fields on a foggy morning.

We all stopped too–the boys looking as bewildered as we were–and for a few seconds I thought Tommy was going to blow for the first time in years.
It wasn't anything like, say, Miss Emily's flappy colour calendars of the English counties.

Well, for a start, Ruth and Tommy had had a serious bust-up.

But Cynthia was a perceptive person, and the fact that she wasn't part of our group just gave her remark more weight.
I saw Harry fleetingly a couple of years ago at the recovery centre in Wiltshire.
I suppose I must have assumed he was raring to go, that I had my work cut out just to hold him off.

There was a bluebottle buzzing around, and for a minute we had a laugh playing “bluebottle tennis,” throwing our hands about to make the demented creature go from one to the other of us.

passages.translation: 每当回想起最后那个夏天，我就会想到那些围着随身听度过的下午。
passages.note: can't ... without ... 表示每当……就会……；用具体物件和共同活动承载对一段时光的回忆。

passages.text: It's time we grew up and started afresh.
How you've got guts and how you always do what you say you're going to do.

It was typical of Tommy that once he knew I was willing to talk, there was suddenly no trace left of any sulkiness; just a kind of grateful eagerness that reminded me of the way we were back in the Juniors when a guardian who'd been telling us off went back to being normal.
In the end I decided to break the deadlock and said: “Tommy, let's talk now.

That she'd done me a big disservice telling me not to worry about being creative.

We didn't know then that all these places had only the most tenuous links with Hailsham.

He'd shown us a list of chores when we'd first arrived, and the students who were already there–“the veterans,” as Hannah called them–had long since worked out a rota which we kept to conscientiously.

Even Ruth looked daunted that sunny day the minibus dropped us in front of the farmhouse, circled round the little pond and disappeared up the slope.

I think about the mornings waking up in my room at the top of the Black Barn to the voices of students outside in the field, arguing about poetry or philosophy; or the long winters, the breakfasts in steamed-up kitchens, meandering discussions around the table about Kafka or Picasso.
In fact, looking back, I see they really went out of their way helping us settle in.
If someone mentions the Cottages today, I think of easy-going days drifting in and out of each other's rooms, the languid way the afternoon would fold into evening then into night.
But then again, when I think about it, there's a sense in which that picture of us on that first day, huddled together in front of the farmhouse, isn't so incongruous after all.
Because maybe, in a way, we didn't leave it behind nearly as much as we might once have thought.
passages.translation: 因为也许，从某种意义上说，我们并没有像曾经以为的那样，把过去远远留在身后。
passages.note: not nearly as much as ... 表示远没有……那么多；maybe 和 in a way 让回望过去的判断保持克制。

passages.text: Back at Hailsham, if a couple were parting, even for a few minutes, it had been an excuse for big embraces and snogging.

There was, incidentally, something I noticed about these veteran couples at the Cottages–something Ruth, for all her close study of them, failed to spot–and this was how so many of their mannerisms were copied from the television.

Once I'd spotted this, I began to notice all kinds of other things the veteran couples had taken from TV programmes: the way they gestured to each other, sat together on sofas, even the way they argued and stormed out of rooms.

Anyway, the thing was, however much we might have fallen out during the day, come bed-time, Ruth and I would still find ourselves sitting side by side on my mattress, sipping our hot drinks, exchanging our deepest feelings about our new life like nothing had ever come between us.

Keffers rummaged in the bag a bit, he didn't know what any of it was–why should he?–and he did this laugh and said no shop he knew would want stuff like that.

We'd been sitting in her room, watching the sunset, as we so often did, enjoying the mineral water and biscuits I'd brought, and I'd been telling her how I still had most of my old Hailsham collection box safely stowed inside my pine chest in my bedsit.
And he could see I was getting a bit emotional, and he changed his tune then.
But it's perhaps stretching it to claim students who'd left were an actual taboo.

passages.translation: 我的意思是，我们每个人当时都在努力适应新的生活；我想，那时候我们都做过后来后悔的事。
passages.note: struggle to adjust to ... 描写适应中的艰难；I suppose 给对他人的理解留出余地。

Sometimes he'd work himself into a complete state–you could see his face under his grey whiskers blotchy with fury–and he'd go thudding around the place, barging into people's rooms without knocking, determined to round up every one of “Steve's magazines.”

When I looked up again, his hands were hovering fretfully in the air, like I was doing a complicated manual task and he was itching to help.
I knew he'd be disappointed I hadn't told him anything, but at that point I hadn't thought things through properly myself and wasn't ready to tell anyone.
When I said I hadn't, she did a laugh and continued: “They're probably just having me on.

For all our little hiccups, Ruth and I had kept up our habit of rounding off the day in my room, talking over our hot drinks, and it was during one of those sessions, when we were larking around about something, that she suddenly said: “I suppose you've heard what Chrissie and Rodney have been saying.”
But I could see she wanted me to drag it out of her, so I kept pressing until in the end she said in a lowered voice: “You remember last week, when Chrissie and Rodney were away?

Though most of us had first come across the idea of “possibles” back at Hailsham, we'd sensed we weren't supposed to discuss it, and so we hadn't–though for sure, it had both intrigued and disturbed us.

Nevertheless, we all of us, to varying degrees, believed that when you saw the person you were copied from, you'd get some insight into who you were deep down, and maybe too, you'd see something of what your life held in store.
The way I remember it, sightings of possibles tended to come in batches.
Weeks could go by with no one mentioning the subject, then one reported sighting would trigger off a whole spate of others.

It was up to each of us to make of our lives what we could.
passages.translation: 我们各自能把自己的生活经营成什么样，要由我们自己去尽力。
passages.note: be up to somebody 表示由某人决定；make of one's life ... 强调如何经营和理解自己的人生。这里是本章人物讨论中的一种看法，不是全书的定论。

passages.text: I can't remember exactly what I said to her that night, but I was at that point pretty sceptical.
But as the weeks had passed, I'd begun to have reservations.
In any discussion, you knew he'd back up Chrissie's angle, and if Chrissie ever said anything mildly amusing, he'd be chortling and shaking his head like he couldn't believe how funny it was.
As I say, my first instinct was not to believe it, and to suppose Chrissie was up to something.
It couldn't last, of course, but like I say, just for those few months, we somehow managed to live in this cosy state of suspension in which we could ponder our lives without the usual boundaries.
Back then, though, I used to just listen, not saying a thing, drinking in their talk.
It was during a bitterly cold spell, and our boxy gas heaters had been giving us trouble.
In fact, listening to her, I even started wondering if maybe it was all feasible: if one day we might all of us move into a place like that and carry on our lives together.
So that was the background to Chrissie and Rodney's claim to have seen Ruth's “possible,” and you can maybe see now why I was wary about it.
Chrissie and Rodney were there that night, of course, hanging onto every word.

The point about Chrissie–and this applied to a lot of the veterans–was that for all her slightly patronising manner towards us when we'd first arrived, she was awestruck about our being from Hailsham.

That day before we went, I remember Ruth and I had been out for a stroll, and we came into the farmhouse kitchen where Fiona and a few veterans were making a huge stew.

That way she could go on talking at least with Chrissie, and Tommy and I could have some sort of conversation to while away the journey.

It was the way she did this, rather than her words, that suddenly made me see things her way; I could see that Ruth was making a big effort to present not just herself, but all of us, in the right way to Chrissie and Rodney; and here I was, threatening to undermine her and start an embarrassing scene.
But now, as we drove on, Ruth stayed more or less silent, sitting right back in her seat, and even when Chrissie or Rodney shouted things to us from the front, responded only in sulky monosyllables.
It had turned into a crisp, sunny day, and my memory of it is that for the first hour we all felt so exhilarated to be out and about we didn't give much thought to what had brought us there.

Then once, when Chrissie made a really obscure reference–she'd said something like: “Oh, yes, the time he put out his jeans!”–Ruth gave a big laugh and signalled in our direction, as though to say to Chrissie: “Go on, explain it to them so they can enjoy it too.”

For a moment, as he said this, the fear passed through me that we'd misjudged things badly; that for all we knew, veterans often used talk of possibles just as a pretext to go on trips, and didn't really expect to take it any further.

And I had a kind of vision of Chrissie and Rodney, back at the Cottages, in the months leading up to this moment, probing and prodding this subject between them.

But I'd heard enough to get the gist of it; and I knew it had specifically to do with us Hailsham students.

passages.note: 用神情消退、转头和呼气三个小动作呈现情绪，不直接替人物下心理结论。

passages.text: Rodney had stayed near the entrance beside a big rack of cards, and further inside, I spotted Tommy under a big pop-group poster, rummaging through the music cassettes.
We walked in silence, Rodney leading the way, through little backstreets hardly penetrated by the sun, the pavements so narrow we often had to shuffle along in single file.
passages.translation: 我们默默走着，由罗德尼带路，穿过阳光几乎照不到的小后街；人行道窄得常常只能排成一列，拖着步子往前走。
passages.note: leading the way 交代伴随状态；hardly penetrated by the sun 和 shuffle along 让场景的逼仄、安静变得可感。

passages.text: As we crossed at a pelican to the sunnier side, I could see Rodney and Chrissie conferring about something and I wondered how much of the bad atmosphere had to do with their believing we were holding back on some big Hailsham secret, and how much was just to do with Ruth's having a go at Tommy.
Both veterans were now standing in the middle of the pavement, letting people with pushchairs move round them, waiting for us to put up a challenge.
Even now, I like places like that: a large store with lots of aisles displaying bright plastic toys, greeting cards, loads of cosmetics, maybe even a photo booth.
Before long, Rodney was looking defensive and on the verge of giving up.
I'd already turned into the aisle–one with fluffy animals and big boxed jigsaws–before I realised Ruth and Chrissie were standing together at the end of it, having some sort of tête-à-tête.
So I just stopped where I was, pretended to examine a jigsaw and waited for them to notice me.
That was when I realised they were back on the subject of this rumour.
People were moving about between desks, or leaning on a partition, chatting and sharing jokes, while others had pulled their swivel chairs close to each other and were enjoying a coffee and sandwich.
But Rodney said quietly, with a tremor of excitement: “There.

Tommy, who had been mucking about on the wall with Rodney, suddenly jumped down and went still.
At times we nearly lost sight of her, but we kept up, loitering in front of window displays when she went into a shop, squeezing past pushchairs and old people when she came out again.
We went on watching her in a kind of trance as she went past on the other side.
Then as she was turning into the High Street, Ruth leapt up and said: “Let's see where she goes.”
We followed along the High Street at a reasonable distance, giggling, dodging past people, separating and coming together again.
And as we kept listening to them, stealing the odd glance in their direction, bit by bit, something started to change.
It was a feeling that grew among us almost tangibly, and I could tell that Ruth, absorbed in a picture on the other side of the room, was feeling it as much as anyone.
You've got to admit, when we saw her through those windows, it did look…” She trailed off, then touched Ruth on the shoulder again.

It's just her letting off steam.

What have we got to lose?”
When I think of that moment now, standing with Tommy in the little side-street about to begin our search, I feel a warmth welling up through me.

passages.translation: 一切忽然都恰到好处：空出的一小时在我们面前铺展开来，再没有比这样度过它更好的方式了。
passages.note: stretching ahead 把时间写成在眼前展开的空间；冒号后用细节解释 perfect。

passages.text: We were just enjoying looking through all those things together; drifting apart then finding ourselves side by side again, maybe competing for the same box of bric-a-brac in a dusty corner lit up by a shaft of sun.

The barn we called the Goosehouse was on the outer fringes of the Cottages, and because the roof leaked badly and the door was permanently off its hinges, it wasn't used for anything much other than as a place for couples to sneak off to in the warmer months.
I turned to see him in his bare feet, perched awkwardly on a bit of dry ground surrounded by huge puddles, one hand on the side of the barn to keep his balance.

The first impression was like one you'd get if you took the back off a radio set: tiny canals, weaving tendons, miniature screws and wheels were all drawn with obsessive precision, and only when you held the page away could you see it was some kind of armadillo, say, or a bird.

passages.text: And I suppose I looked at him with resignation, with a face that said: “Yes, it's true, what else did you expect?”
All I can say is that at the time what I feared more than anything was that one or the other of them would stalk off first, and I'd be left with the remaining one.

It never occurred to me that our lives, until then so closely interwoven, could unravel and separate over a thing like that.
I had this idea at the time–and I was probably right–that if our sense of the essays being important was allowed to seep away, then so too would whatever bound us together as Hailsham students.

passages.text: In the centre of the room, under the chandelier, as became a host, stood the head of the family, old Jolyon himself.
passages.translation: 在房间中央的枝形吊灯下面，如主人身份所宜，站着这个家族的首领——老Jolyon本人。

passages.text: rapid, shifting scrutiny of surrounding facts
passages.translation: 对周围情况迅速而游移不定的审视

passages.text: a man of poor constitution
passages.translation: 一个体质虚弱的男人

passages.text: seemed master of perennial youth
passages.translation: 似乎拥有长驻的青春

passages.text: Having had his own way for innumerable years, he had earned a prescriptive right to it.
passages.translation: 多年来凡事都随自己的心意，他仿佛已由此取得了这样做的当然权利。

passages.text: They could not have explained the origin of a misgiving obscured by the mist of family gossip.
passages.translation: 他们也说不清被家族闲话的迷雾遮蔽的这种疑虑从何而来。

passages.text: so these unconscious artists—the Forsytes—had fastened by intuition on this hat
passages.translation: 于是这些不自觉的艺术家——Forsyte一家——凭直觉紧紧盯住了这顶帽子

passages.text: The hat had obviously been worn as a practical joke! He himself was a connoisseur of such.
passages.translation: 戴那顶帽子显然是为了搞恶作剧！他自己正是这类事情的行家。

passages.text: the favourite mode of alluding to Bosinney
passages.translation: 间接提到Bosinney时最爱用的说法

passages.text: his sweet and tentative obstinacy
passages.translation: 他那温和而试探性的固执

passages.text: a sign of something ineradicable in the family soul
passages.translation: 家族灵魂中某种根深蒂固之物的迹象

passages.text: a strange, disreputable cat
passages.translation: 一只陌生而不体面的猫

passages.text: the significant trifle
passages.translation: 那个意味深长的小细节

passages.text: Her aunts reproached June afterwards about the hat.
passages.translation: 她的几位姑婆后来为了那顶帽子的事责备了June。

passages.text: June had answered in her imperious brisk way
passages.translation: June已用她那强硬而利落的方式作了回答

passages.text: like the little embodiment of will she was
passages.translation: 正像她本来就是的那个意志的小小化身

passages.text: Mrs Soames had actually given up wearing feathers, so dreadfully downright was dear June!
passages.translation: Mrs Soames竟然真的不再佩戴羽毛了，可见亲爱的June说话是多么直白得吓人！

passages.text: they stood head to head and shoulder to shoulder
passages.translation: 他们头挨着头、肩并着肩站着

passages.text: June, old Jolyon’s acknowledged heiress
passages.translation: June，Old Jolyon的公认女继承人

passages.text: Timothy’s commodious, red-brick residence in Bayswater
passages.translation: Timothy在Bayswater那所宽敞的红砖住宅

passages.text: Looks as if he might make a bolt of it—the dashing Buccaneer!
passages.translation: 看上去他倒像要溜之大吉呢——这位潇洒的海盗！

passages.text: He had sherry-coloured eyes, disconcertingly inattentive at times.
passages.translation: 他有一双雪利酒颜色的眼睛，有时心不在焉得令人不自在。

passages.text: I dunno what to make of ’im.
passages.translation: 我可不知道该怎么看他。

passages.text: Looks to me for all the world like an ’alf-tame leopard.
passages.translation: 在我看来，他简直像一头半驯服的豹。

passages.text: June stood in front, fending off this idle curiosity
passages.translation: June站在前面，挡开这些无聊的好奇打量

passages.text: And every now and then a Forsyte would come up, sidle round, and take a look at him.
passages.translation: 不时就有一个Forsyte家的成员走上前来，侧着身子绕过来打量他一番。

passages.text: very singular-looking man
passages.translation: 模样非常奇特的人

passages.text: He was seldom, indeed, far from Irene’s side at public functions, and even when separated by the exigencies of social intercourse, could be seen following her about with his eyes, in which were strange expressions of watchfulness and longing.
passages.translation: 的确，在公开社交场合，他很少远离伊琳身边；即使因社交应酬的需要而与她分开，也可以看见他的目光追随着她，眼中带着异样的警觉与渴望。

passages.text: She made no reply, for she rarely spoke, husbanding her aged voice; but to James, uneasy of conscience, her look was as good as an answer.
passages.translation: 她没有作答，因为她很少开口，省着用自己衰老的嗓音；但对心中不安的詹姆斯而言，她的目光就等于回答。

passages.text: he got quite thin dancing attendance on her
passages.translation: 他围着她献殷勤，竟瘦了不少

passages.text: James interrupted her reverie
passages.translation: 詹姆斯打断了她的遐想

passages.text: ‘No, he had not thought it wise, with so much of this diphtheria about; and he so liable to take things.’
passages.translation: “没有，近来白喉这么多，他觉得来不明智；何况他又这么容易染上病。”

passages.text: he had some years before, when business was at full tide, scented out the stagnation which, indeed, had not yet come
passages.translation: 几年前，在生意正兴旺时，他便已嗅到了那场当时其实尚未到来的停滞

passages.text: the stagnation which, indeed, had not yet come, but which ultimately, as all agreed, was bound to set in
passages.translation: 那场停滞当时确实尚未到来，但大家都认为，它终究必然会出现

passages.text: had invested the quite conspicuous proceeds in three per cent Consols
passages.translation: 已把那笔相当可观的所得款项投入利率为百分之三的英国统一公债

passages.text: a spirit perhaps better than commonly endowed with caution
passages.translation: 一种或许比常人更具谨慎天性的精神

passages.text: they quailed before her incorruptible figure
passages.translation: 他们在她那不可动摇的身影面前畏缩

passages.text: a kind of incarnation of security
passages.translation: 某种安全感的化身

passages.text: done for himself by deserting his wife and child and running away with that foreign governess
passages.translation: 因抛下妻子和孩子、与那个外国女家庭教师出走而断送了自己的前途

passages.text: a dapper, clean-shaven man, with hardly a hair on his head
passages.translation: 一个衣着整洁利落、胡须刮得干干净净、头上几乎没什么头发的男人

passages.text: the look of a preternaturally sage schoolboy
passages.translation: 一个老成得异乎寻常的小学生的神情

passages.text: Each brother wore an air of aggravation as he looked at the other two, knowing by experience that they would try to eclipse his ailments.
passages.translation: 每个兄弟看着另外两人时都一脸恼火，凭经验知道他们会设法把他的病痛比下去。

passages.text: the look of a preternaturally sage schoolboy
passages.translation: 一副聪明老成得异乎寻常的小学生模样

passages.text: Indulgent and severe was her look.
passages.translation: 她的目光既宽厚又严厉。

passages.text: ‘Want of exercise,’ muttered James, his eyes on the china.
passages.translation: “缺乏运动，”詹姆斯望着那件瓷器，低声嘟囔道。

passages.text: her resolute small face
passages.translation: 她那张神情坚定的小脸

passages.text: The old lady’s round, steel-grey eyes, over which a film like a bird’s was beginning to come, followed her wistfully amongst the bustling crowd
passages.translation: 老太太那双圆圆的、钢灰色的眼睛，正开始像鸟眼那样蒙上一层薄翳，带着眷恋在人群中追随着她

passages.text: Amongst the throng of people by the door
passages.translation: 在门边聚集的人群中

passages.text: she saw only her own flesh and blood
passages.translation: 她眼里只有自己的骨肉亲人

passages.text: Still, he had forfeited his right to be there
passages.translation: 尽管如此，他已经丧失了在那里出现的权利

passages.text: she kissed the girl’s cheek with trembling fervour
passages.translation: 她带着颤抖的热情，吻了吻女孩的脸颊

passages.text: The thought rankled with the bitterness of a long-inflicted injury in her tenacious old heart.
passages.translation: 这念头在她那颗执拗的老心里刺痛着，带着一桩早年所受伤害的苦涩。

passages.text: He spoke with relish, as though he felt that he was cheering up his old aunt.
passages.translation: 他说得津津有味，仿佛觉得自己正在让老姑妈开心起来。

passages.text: stealthily wetting his finger and rubbing it on the knobby bulbs
passages.translation: 悄悄弄湿手指，在那些凸起的圆结上摩擦

passages.text: Capital position, not two minutes from me
passages.translation: 地段好极了，离我那儿还不到两分钟的路程

passages.text: Their father, of farming stock, had come from Dorsetshire near the beginning of the century.
passages.translation: 他们的父亲出身农家，在本世纪初前后从多塞特郡迁来。

passages.text: not much refinement about him
passages.translation: 他身上没有多少文雅气质

passages.text: a cart track rutted into the pink earth
passages.translation: 一条在粉红色泥土上轧出车辙的车道

passages.text: The stream which worked the mill came bubbling down in a dozen rivulets
passages.translation: 带动磨坊的溪水分成十来股细流，潺潺地流下来

passages.text: The stream which worked the mill came bubbling down in a dozen rivulets, and pigs were hunting round that estuary.
passages.translation: 带动磨坊的溪水分成十来股细流，潺潺地流下来，猪就在那个河口周围觅食。

passages.text: he came back to town in a poor way, and went about with a pathetic attempt at making the best of a bad job.
passages.translation: 他情绪低落地回到城里，可怜巴巴地试着把这桩不如意的事往好处想。

passages.text: regular country little place, old as the hills.
passages.translation: 一个十足的乡间小地方，古老得不得了。

passages.text: Yeomen—I suppose very small beer.
passages.translation: 自耕农——我想也就是些很不起眼的小人物。

passages.text: From their father, the builder, they inherited a talent for bricks and mortar.
passages.translation: 他们从做建筑商的父亲那里，继承了与房屋打交道的本领。

passages.text: he came back to town in a poor way
passages.translation: 他情绪低落地回到城里

passages.text: He himself had had his eye on a house there for the last two years, but they wanted such a price.
passages.translation: 他自己这两年来一直看中那儿的一幢房子，可是对方的要价实在太高。

passages.text: Twenty-two years to run?
passages.translation: 租期还剩二十二年？

passages.text: ‘I don’t,’ said old Jolyon, ‘care a fig for his opinion.’
passages.translation: “他的意见，”老乔里恩说，“我一点也不在乎。”

passages.text: He went down to the front door and saw them into their barouche, and twinkled at them, having already forgotten his spleen
passages.translation: 他走下去来到前门，把他们送上四轮敞篷马车，又笑眯眯地望着他们，早已忘了刚才的怒气

passages.text: Soames, glancing at her beneath his eyelids, nodded, and he saw Irene steal at him one of her unfathomable looks.
passages.translation: 索姆斯从眼皮底下朝她瞥了一眼，点点头，又看见伊琳悄悄向他投来她那种难以捉摸的眼神。

passages.text: the very house I was after—you’ve given too much for it!
passages.translation: 就是我看中的那幢房子——你买得太贵了！

passages.text: I’m told they don’t get on.
passages.translation: 我听说他们合不来。

passages.text: his light grey eyes measured the street frontage of the houses by the way
passages.translation: 他那浅灰色的眼睛估量着沿途房屋的临街面宽度

passages.text: Soames will have trouble with her; you mark my words, he’ll have trouble—she’s got a foreign look.
passages.translation: 索姆斯准会因为她遇上麻烦；你记住我的话，他准会遇上麻烦——她有一种异国人的模样。

passages.text: She must cost him a pretty penny in dress!
passages.translation: 她穿衣打扮一定要花他一大笔钱！

passages.text: I call her distinguished-looking
passages.translation: 我说她是仪表不凡

passages.text: Each felt aggrieved that the other had not modified his habits to secure his society a little longer
passages.translation: 两人都感到委屈，觉得对方不肯改变自己的习惯，好再和自己多待一会儿

passages.text: Cantankerous chap Roger always was!
passages.translation: 罗杰一向就是个难相处的家伙！

passages.text: There was little sentimentality about the Forsytes.
passages.translation: Forsyte一家很少感情用事。

passages.text: This was the occasion of an ‘At Home’ to celebrate the engagement of Miss June Forsyte, old Jolyon’s granddaughter, to Mr Philip Bosinney.
passages.translation: 这次家庭招待会，是为了庆祝Old Jolyon的孙女June Forsyte小姐与Philip Bosinney先生订婚。

passages.text: I made him bring every penny into settlement
passages.translation: 我要求他把每一分钱都纳入婚姻财产安排。
